root_cause.text: In io_uring's __io_uring_show_fdinfo() SQE_MIXED handling, the wraparound check used ++sq_head instead of the real ring index (sq_idx = (i + sq_head) & sq_mask), so 128-byte SQEs at the last sq_sqes slot could bypass the boundary check and trigger an out-of-bounds read of the second half.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states “sq_head is only incremented when a 128-byte SQE is encountered, not on every iteration” and “The actual array index is sq_idx = (i + sq_head) & sq_mask, which can be sq_mask (the last slot) while the wrap check passes”; the patch changes `if ((++sq_head & sq_mask) == 0)` to `if (sq_idx == sq_mask)` and only increments `sq_head` afterward.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the 128-byte SQE wraparound corruption check so it does not incorrectly advance `sq_head` while validating the last ring entry.
intent_record.what: The conditional check was changed from testing `(++sq_head & sq_mask) == 0` to testing `sq_idx == sq_mask`, and the increment of `sq_head` was moved out of the condition into a separate `sq_head++;` statement after the corruption check.
intent_record.how: This prevents `sq_head` from being incremented as a side effect of evaluating the wraparound corruption check, so the code now detects a 128-byte SQE wrapping at the last ring index without prematurely advancing the submission queue head and altering iteration state.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the 128-byte SQE wraparound corruption check so it does not incorrectly advance `sq_head` while validating the last ring entry.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the faulty 128-byte SQE wraparound check in SQE_MIXED handling by avoiding incorrect ++sq_head advancement when validating the last ring entry, which is the stated root cause of the out-of-bounds read.

candidates.rationale: This is the faulty wraparound check described in the root cause. It advances sq_head and checks that mutated value instead of validating wraparound using the actual ring index for the current SQE slot, allowing a 128-byte SQE at the last slot to bypass the boundary check and cause an out-of-bounds read.

vuln_statements.explanation: This wraparound check is the root cause: it increments and tests sq_head itself instead of checking wraparound based on the actual SQE ring index for the current entry. For a 128-byte SQE in the last slot, this can incorrectly miss the boundary condition and allow reading the second half past the ring buffer boundary.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it contains the exact SQE_MIXED handling and boundary check logic in __io_uring_show_fdinfo(). The vulnerable construct is present in the new mixed-SQE path: after reading `sq_idx = READ_ONCE(ctx->sq_array[sq_head & sq_mask]);` and `sqe = &ctx->sq_sqes[sq_idx << sq_shift];`, the code checks for a 128B mixed SQE with `else if (io_issue_defs[opcode].is_128) { ... }`. Inside that block, the wraparound test is `if ((++sq_head & sq_mask) == 0) { ... corrupted sqe, wrapping 128B entry ... break; }`. This uses `++sq_head` rather than validating based on the actual ring slot index used for the SQE (`sq_idx`, or equivalently the real ring position). That matches the stated root cause: the check is based on incrementing the head counter instead of the true ring index, so a 128-byte SQE located at the last `sq_sqes` slot can evade the boundary validation and then later be treated as `sqe128 = true`, causing the second half access via `u64 *sqeb = (void *) (sqe + 1);`. There is no corrected check here based on `sq_idx` / actual ring position before dereferencing `(sqe + 1)`, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the SQE dumping logic inside `__io_uring_show_fdinfo()` and the handling for 128-byte SQEs. The root cause was that SQE128 handling used the wrong wraparound/boundary logic and did not correctly account for doubled SQE size. In this commit, the function explicitly adds `unsigned int sq_shift = 0;` and sets it with `if (ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_SQE128) sq_shift = 1;`, showing awareness of SQE128. More importantly, when fetching the SQE, it now uses `sqe = &ctx->sq_sqes[sq_idx << 1];`, which shifts the SQE index by 1 for 128-byte SQEs as described in the commit message. The extended half is only dumped under `if (sq_shift) { u64 *sqeb = (void *) (sqe + 1); ... }`, meaning the code intentionally accesses the second half only in SQE128 mode after selecting the doubled-size base entry. This matches the fix described by the commit message ('need to shift the sq index by 1'). The vulnerable construct described in the root cause—using an incorrect wraparound progression like `++sq_head` instead of the real ring-derived index for checking the second half—is not present in this shown function body.
